q1_issues.issue: The event noun "destruction" is classed as the verb lemma `destroy`, which is derivation across parts of speech, forbidden by the lemmatization rule ("inflection only — never derivation"); the surface noun is no longer recoverable.

q2_gaps: a deverbal event nominalization as the object of a causation verb ("causes the destruction") — nothing says whether such an NP reifies an eventuality at top level or stays a plain typed entity

objective "of"-genitive argument of an event noun ("the destruction of the archive") — no rule for attaching a nominalization's argument; the genitive section covers only genuinely possessive of-phrases and the light-verb section covers only occurred/happened/took place
notes: Otherwise the licensed causation-verb shape: "cause" is an ordinary event with Agent = fire and the complement eventuality reified at top level under Theme, with no tense on either event.
